title: False imprisonment is unlawful and intentional restraint of a person's freedom of movement within a bounded area

content.overview: False imprisonment is unlawful and intentional restraint of a person's freedom of movement within a bounded area. Complete restraint is required; physical force, actual awareness and measurable financial loss are not always necessary.
content.glance: False imprisonment is unlawful and intentional restraint of a person's freedom of movement within a bounded area. Complete restraint is required; physical force, actual awareness and measurable financial loss are not always necessary.
content.study: False imprisonment is unlawful and intentional restraint of a person's freedom of movement within a bounded area. Complete restraint is required; physical force, actual awareness and measurable financial loss are not always necessary.\n\nThe tort protects personal liberty. Bird v Jones establishes that obstruction of one route while another reasonable route remains open is not complete confinement. Indian constitutional jurisprudence adds a separate public-law dimension to unlawful detention under Article 21.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The tort protects personal liberty. Bird v Jones establishes that obstruction of one route while another reasonable route remains open is not complete confinement. Indian constitutional jurisprudence adds a separate public-law dimension to unlawful detention under Article 21.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: The common-law tort recognises restraint by barriers, threats or asserted authority. Lawful arrest or detention is a defence unless the authority is exceeded or unlawfully exercised.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Complete restraint within defined limits. 2. Intention to restrain or conduct attributable to defendant. 3. No lawful justification. 4. Causal connection. Actual financial loss is not a necessary element.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Detention records, CCTV, witness testimony, messages and official documents may establish confinement. Public-law detention cases require careful scrutiny of custody and arrest records.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Ordinary claims are civil. Constitutional detention may invoke habeas corpus or public-law compensation. The forum depends on relief sought and limitation must be checked for the specific cause of action.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: Complete restraint is essential to the common-law tort; constitutional compensation for unlawful detention is analytically distinct. The claimant must still prove the remaining ingredients on the civil standard.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: Confinement may be created by barriers, threats or asserted authority without physical force. A court should not infer liability from the label alone.
